newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends at 18 month high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends at 18 month high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended sharply higher Tuesday, mostly on fund buying on a breakout of a six week 11.40-12.00 cent a lb range for the October contract, traders said.

"The move looked awfully technical in nature, led by fund buying, and does not appear to have much immediate support from the fundamentals, apart from some concern about possible hurricane damage to the domestic U.S. crop," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said.
CSCE October world sugar ended up 0.40 cent at 12.18 cents, after seeing an intraday high at 12.20 cents.

October sugar saw its highest level since January 1995, when it saw a contract high at 12.50 cents, but on the continuation chart for nearby sugar, the rally would have to clear the 12.85 cent level seen in late June to confirm a resumption of the long term 1991-1995 uptrend, analysts said.
While October sugar remains the active contract, with open interest of 69,474 lots, the contract expires on September 30 and open interest is rising in the March 1997 contract.
March sugar ended up 0.28 cent at 11.71 cents, after breaking out of a six week 11.10-11.50 range and rallying to a a life-of-contract high at 11.75 cents.
